events.title: Less CSS preprocessor introduced
events.summary: Alexis Sellier introduced the Less CSS preprocessor on June 16, 2009 via the 'Introducing LESS' blog post — keeping standard CSS syntax while adding variables and mixins.
events.about: Less extended CSS with `@variable` declarations, nested rules, and mixins — all valid CSS with extra features on top. Inspired by Sass but written in JavaScript, it lowered the barrier for developers who wanted preprocessor power without learning a new indented syntax. Bootstrap adopted Less before moving to Sass.

narrative.whyChosen: Less proved preprocessors could feel like CSS with braces, not a separate language.
narrative.whyImportant: It pushed Sass toward SCSS and made preprocessor workflows mainstream in JavaScript toolchains.
narrative.problemSolved: Sass's indented syntax felt alien to developers used to curly-brace CSS.

events.title: iPhone 3GS released
events.summary: Apple began selling the iPhone 3GS on June 19, 2009 — adding a faster processor, video recording, and voice control.
events.about: The 3GS refined the iPhone platform with substantially better performance and a 3-megapixel video camera. Developers gained headroom for richer games and media apps while mobile Safari improved with better JavaScript performance.

narrative.whyChosen: The 3GS proved Apple's 'S' year could deliver meaningful speed and camera upgrades without a redesign.
narrative.whyImportant: Faster hardware made native iOS apps feel responsive enough for console-style games and video workflows.
narrative.problemSolved: Early iPhones struggled with sluggish UI and limited multimedia capture for mainstream users.

events.title: Nokia N97 released
events.summary: Nokia released the Nokia N97 — touchscreen Symbian with slide-out keyboard — late Symbian flagship.
events.about: Nokia hardware shaped pre-iPhone smartphones and later Microsoft's mobile platform bet. Touchscreen symbian with slide-out keyboard — late symbian flagship.

narrative.whyChosen: The Nokia N97 was a flagship Nokia smartphone milestone.
narrative.whyImportant: Nokia devices defined mobile platforms from Symbian through Windows Phone.
narrative.problemSolved: Mobile users needed capable smartphones before the iPhone/Android era matured.

events.title: PHP 5.3 released
events.summary: PHP 5.3 shipped on June 30, 2009 with namespaces, closures, and late static binding — modernizing the language for frameworks.
events.about: Namespaces (`namespace App\Model`) let Symfony, Laravel, and Composer coexist without class name collisions. Closures and `use` imports enabled functional patterns in PHP. PHP 5.3 was the foundation for the framework renaissance of the 2010s.

narrative.whyChosen: PHP 5.3 added the language features enterprise PHP frameworks required.
narrative.whyImportant: Namespaces unlocked PSR standards and Composer's package ecosystem.
narrative.problemSolved: Global class names and weak OOP primitives made large PHP codebases fragile.
